mainTopic: The stolen טבל and the תרומה case, then a new משנה on a wife's vow not to work, with שמואל's ruling and the question of דבר שלא בא לעולם.
overview: The amud continues a question about the משנה: may כהנים take תרומה from a man who forbade all כהנים to benefit from him? The גמרא first tries to tie the two halves of the משנה to a ברייתא about a thief who stole טבל. In that ברייתא, רבי says the thief pays for everything and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה says he pays only for the חולין. The גמרא suggests they argue about whether טובת הנאה counts as money. It then concludes that both opinions are really a קנס: רבי fines the thief, and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה fines the owner for delaying the separation of his טבל. רבא gives a different answer: תרומה is special, because once it is forbidden to all כהנים it is worthless. A new משנה follows, about a wife who vows not to work for relatives or for her husband, with the opinions of רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי. שמואל rules like רבי יוחנן בן נורי. The גמרא asks whether this means a person can make holy something that does not exist yet, and it begins a contradiction from a משנה in כתובות that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Is the dispute about whether the owner's choice is worth money?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה argue about whether טובת הנאה has monetary value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that רבי holds that the owner's right to choose who gets the gifts is worth money, and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה holds that it is not worth money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to settle an apparent contradiction between the two halves of the משנה by tying them to a dispute between תנאים. It suggests that the dispute about a thief who stole טבל is really a dispute about טובת הנאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If טובת הנאה is money, the owner has a real money stake in the תרומה and מעשרות inside the טבל, so the thief must pay for everything (רבי). If it is not money, the owner owns only the חולין part, so the thief pays only for that (רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה).

keyTerms.meaning: The owner's benefit of choosing which כהן or לוי receives his gifts
Produce whose תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been separated

phrases.english: That Rabbi holds:
phrases.notes: This finishes the question from just before: "Isn't it that they argue about this?" רבי here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: the benefit of discretion is money,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, holds:
the benefit of discretion is not money?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the attempt, begun just before this amud, to resolve the contradiction in the משנה (כהנים take תרומה against his will vs. other כהנים take it) by showing the two clauses match two תנאים in the ברייתא of the stolen טבל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dispute about the thief depends on whether טובת הנאה has monetary value.

steps.title: Everyone agrees the owner's choice is not money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone agrees טובת הנאה is not money, so the argument is about gifts that were not yet separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that the owner's choice is not worth money. Here they argue about gifts that have not yet been separated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the suggestion from step 1 and offers a different point of disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both sides agree about טובת הנאה. The new idea is that they argue about whether gifts that were never separated count as if they were already separated. If they count as separated, the thief pays only for the חולין part.

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts for the כהן and לוי (תרומה and מעשרות)

phrases.english: No, for everyone agrees
the benefit of discretion is not money.
Rather, here, regarding gifts
that were not separated, they disagree.
phrases.notes: In other words, do gifts still sitting inside the טבל count as if they were already taken out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the טובת הנאה explanation and replaces it with a dispute about unseparated gifts.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects טובת הנאה as the point of disagreement.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both opinions agree טובת הנאה is not money, so it cannot be the root of the dispute.

steps.title: Then why should separation matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new explanation: if טובת הנאה is not money, separating the gifts or not should make no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the owner's choice is not worth money, what difference does it make whether the gifts were separated or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation it just gave in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner has no money rights in the gifts, then the תרומה and מעשרות were never his, whether they are still inside the טבל or already taken out. So the question of 'separated or not' cannot change how much the thief pays.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is it to me

phrases.english: But if the benefit of discretion is not money,
what difference is it to me if they were separated,
what difference is it to me if they were not separated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation offered in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the dispute is about unseparated gifts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once טובת הנאה is not money, the owner owns none of the gifts either way, so separation cannot matter.

steps.title: Both opinions are penalties: one on the thief, one on the owner
steps.stepSummary: The real reason: רבי says the רבנן penalized the thief, and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה says they penalized the owner for delaying the separation of his טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is רבי's reason: the רבנן fined the thief so he won't steal. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה holds that the רבנן fined the owner so he won't delay separating the gifts from his טבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final explanation. The dispute is not about who owns the gifts but about whom the רבנן chose to penalize.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the owner does not really own the gifts. רבי makes the thief pay for everything as a קנס so he will not steal again. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה lets the owner collect only for the חולין as a קנס, because he left his produce as טבל too long.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees טובת הנאה is not money. The argument about the stolen טבל is about a קנס: רבי fines the thief so he won't steal, and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה fines the owner so he won't delay separating his gifts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a payment rule can come from a rabbinic penalty rather than from actual ownership. The two opinions differ only on which person deserves the fine.

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason of Rabbi:
the Rabbis penalized the thief
so that he will not steal.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, holds:
the Rabbis penalized the owner,
so that he will not delay with his untithed produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by moving the dispute away from ownership and onto a rabbinic penalty.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-explains both opinions as different קנסות rather than a dispute about ownership.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute depended on טובת הנאה or on whether unseparated gifts count as separated.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree the owner does not own the gifts. The dispute is whether the רבנן fined the thief or the owner.

steps.title: רבא: תרומה Is Different Because It Becomes Worthless
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that תרומה is a special case. Once the owner forbids it to all כהנים, it has no use to anyone, so taking it gives the כהנים no benefit from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: תרומה is different. The reason the כהנים may take it against his will is that תרומה is only usable by כהנים. Since he is trying to forbid it to them, he has made it like plain dust.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different way to settle the contradiction between the two halves of the משנה. He does not split them between two תנאים. Instead he says the first case, where כהנים take the תרומה against his will, comes from something special about תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only כהנים may eat תרומה. If the owner forbids it to all of them, it becomes useless, and he has basically thrown it away. So when the כהנים take it, they are not getting any benefit from him, even if טובת הנאה would normally be worth money.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן, which only כהנים may eat
It is not fit or usable

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the כהנים may take the תרומה because forbidding it to all of them makes it worthless to its owner. Nothing of his is left for them to benefit from.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explanation does not depend on whether טובת הנאה counts as money. The answer comes only from the special nature of תרומה.

phrases.english: Rava said: Teruma is different,
for this is the reason that they may take it against his will:
phrases.notes: "They" are the כהנים, in the case where the owner forbade all כהנים from benefiting from him.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דִּתְרוּמָה לָא חַזְיָא אֶלָּא לְכֹהֲנִים,
phrases.english: because teruma is fit only for kohanim,
and since he comes to forbid it to them,
he has made it like mere dust.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 4 showed that the stolen-טבל dispute is about a קנס and not about טובת הנאה, the attempt to split the משנה between two תנאים falls away. רבא then resolves the משנה's contradiction differently: the whole משנה can hold טובת הנאה is money, and the תרומה case is an exception because forbidden תרומה is worthless.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהנים may take the תרומה only because טובת הנאה has no money value.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if טובת הנאה has money value, תרומה forbidden to all כהנים is worthless, so taking it gives no benefit from the owner.

steps.title: A Wife's Vow Not to Work for Relatives or for Her Husband
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. If a wife vows not to work for her father, his father, her brother, or his brother, the husband cannot cancel the vow. If she vows not to work for him, he does not need to cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she said, 'It is קונם that I will not work for my father,' or 'for your father,' or 'for my brother,' or 'for your brother,' he cannot cancel it. If she said, 'I will not work for you,' he does not need to cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It compares a wife's vow not to work for relatives with a vow not to work for her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband can only cancel certain kinds of vows. A vow about working for relatives is not one of them, so he cannot cancel it. A vow not to work for him cannot take effect, because she is already obligated to do that work. So it does not need to be cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used to make a נדר, a substitute for קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: "אינו יכול להפר" (he cannot cancel) and "אינו צריך להפר" (he does not need to cancel) sound alike but mean very different things. In the first case the vow stands. In the second case the vow never takes effect at all.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ ״קֻוֽנָּם שֶׁאֵינִי עוֹשָׂה עַל פִּי אַבָּא״,
phrases.english: MISHNA: "It is konam that I will not work for my father,"
phrases.notes: A wife is the one speaking here. "עושה על פי" means doing work for someone.

phrases.aramaic: וְ״עַל פִּי אָבִיךָ״, וְ״עַל פִּי אָחִי״,
phrases.english: or "for your father," or "for my brother,"

phrases.aramaic: וְ״עַל פִּי אָחִיךָ״ — אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהָפֵר.
phrases.english: or "for your brother": he cannot cancel it.
"That I will not work for you":
he does not need to cancel it.

steps.triggerLanguage: קֻוֽנָּם שֶׁאֵינִי עוֹשָׂה עַל פִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband cannot cancel her vow not to work for relatives. A vow not to work for him has no effect, so no cancellation is needed.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: Cancel It in Case She Does Extra Work
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the husband should cancel the vow anyway. She might do more work than she owes, and the vow would apply to that extra work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: He should cancel it, because perhaps she will do more for him than he is entitled to.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with the משנה's last ruling. He says the husband should still cancel the vow "I will not work for you."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow does not apply to work she owes him. But if she does extra work beyond that, the vow does apply to the extra, and he would be benefiting from forbidden work. Cancelling the vow removes that risk.

keyTerms.meaning: She will do extra, beyond what is required

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: He should cancel it,
because perhaps she will do extra for him
more than he is entitled to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה about the vow "I will not work for you."
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband should cancel the vow, because it applies to any extra work beyond what she owes him.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: Cancel It in Case He Divorces Her
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי also says to cancel the vow, but for a different reason. If he divorces her, the vow would take effect and she would be forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: He should cancel it, because perhaps he will divorce her and she will be forbidden to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי agrees that the husband should cancel the vow, but he gives a different worry. He is concerned about what happens after a divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While they are married, her work belongs to him, so the vow cannot take effect. After a divorce she no longer owes him anything, so the vow would take effect. He could then never remarry her, because he would be benefiting from her work.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי agree he should cancel the vow, even though right now it has no effect. רבי עקיבא worries about extra work she might do. רבי יוחנן בן נורי worries about remarrying her after a divorce.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר: יָפֵר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says: He should cancel it,
because perhaps he will divorce her
and she will be forbidden to him.
phrases.notes: He means he could not remarry her, since he would then benefit from her work, which the vow forbids.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר: יָפֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with רבי עקיבא that the husband should cancel the vow, but gives a different reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband should cancel the vow, because after a divorce it would take effect and prevent him from remarrying her.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with שמואל's ruling: the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל said: The הלכה is like רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section on the משנה begins. שמואל gives a ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said the husband should cancel the vow, because if he divorces her the vow would take effect and she would be forbidden to him. שמואל agrees with this view as the practical הלכה. This ruling is the starting point for the questions that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
The practical Jewish law, how we actually rule
A major early אמורא from Babylonia

phrases.english: Gemara: Shmuel said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the opinion of רבי יוחנן בן נורי from the משנה (Step 8).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי: the husband should cancel the vow, since it could take effect after a divorce.

steps.title: Does שמואל hold one can make holy something not yet existing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל's ruling means he holds that a person can make holy something that does not exist yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that שמואל holds that a person can make holy something that has not yet come into the world?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from שמואל's ruling and asks if it is correct. This sets up a contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, her vow takes hold of work she will only do after a divorce. That work does not exist yet, so it is a דבר שלא בא לעולם. If שמואל rules this way, it seems he holds that a vow or הקדש can take hold of something that does not exist yet.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is this to say...?": the גמרא is drawing a conclusion from what was just said
He holds, he is of the opinion
Makes something holy (הקדש), or forbids it with a vow
Something that does not exist yet

steps.confusionAlert: The work the wife does now is not the issue. The question is about work she will do after a divorce, which does not exist yet.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether a vow or הקדש can take hold of something that does not exist yet is a major topic across ש״ס, and it decides how we understand שמואל's ruling.

phrases.english: Is this to say that Shmuel holds

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לְעוֹלָם?
phrases.english: a person can consecrate something that has not yet come into the world?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general idea out of שמואל's ruling in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does שמואל's ruling mean he holds אדם מקדיש דבר שלא בא לעולם?

steps.title: Contradiction from consecrating a wife's earnings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to quote a משנה about a man who makes his wife's earnings holy. It will use this משנה to contradict the conclusion about שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contradicted this from a משנה: One who consecrates his wife's earnings...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a source that seems to clash with what we just said about שמואל. This line only sets up the challenge, and the rest of the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רמינהי means a contradiction is coming from another source. The case is about a husband making holy his wife's future earnings, which also do not exist yet. How that משנה rules will be compared with שמואל's position.

keyTerms.meaning: "And they threw them together": a contradiction is raised from another source
His wife's earnings, the work she produces

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: One who consecrates his wife's earnings —
phrases.notes: The quote is from a משנה in כתובות and continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a contradiction against the conclusion drawn in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that שמואל holds a person can make holy something not yet existing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about making a wife's future earnings holy will be shown to clash with that position. The full wording continues in the next section.
